headline: Wood pyrolysis demonstration project at McNeil recommended, with Vermont Renewable Gas as developer
summary: The project would use a 2.2 megawatt unit at McNeil under a 20-year power purchase agreement, and the proposal goes next to the Board of Finance and City Council. Staff said the developer would finance, permit, own and run it, producing about 18,480 megawatt-hours a year and cutting stack CO2 per unit of energy by around 60%. Public speakers raised concerns about emissions and fire risk. Seven tariff changes were also recommended, and a property insurance renewal of up to $741,500 was approved.
decisions: Recommended seven tariff changes and new programs to the City Council, including a new battery storage pilot.
Recommended the wood pyrolysis project to the Board of Finance and City Council as presented, 4-0.
Approved the property, boiler and machinery insurance renewal for November 20, 2026 to November 20, 2027, with a premium of up to $741,500, 4-0.
discussion: Wood pyrolysis project: Staff described heating wood in an oxygen-poor chamber to make syngas for power and biochar. Staff said it would use about 12% less wood than McNeil for the same output. Public speakers questioned the emissions figures, fire risk, and whether the technology could scale.

Project economics: Staff said the project breaks even only under a high forecast of energy, capacity, REC, and transmission values. Commissioners asked about the contract terms, which were discussed in executive session.
Tariff package: Staff said most changes align tariffs with the new billing system. For the home EV charging rate, staff estimated about $22,000 in added credits a year.

Efficiency targets: Energy services staff said some 2024 to 2026 performance targets would be missed, and that the utility asked the PUC for goal adjustments. Staff cited inflation, construction delays, and the mercury bulb ban as reasons for lower savings.

decision_evidence.quote: Burlington Electric Department requests that the Electric Commission recommend the City Council approve its filing of several tariff amendments, a new tariff rate proposal, and a new pilot program with the Vermont Public Utility Commission. ... Okay, that passes.
I move to approve and recommend the wood pyrolysis proposal to Board of Finance, City Council, as presented. ... Okay, it passes 4 to 0.

I move to authorize the general manager of Burlington Electric Department or their designee to execute the property boiler and machinery insurance coverage renewal contract with AIG Zurich StarTech Aegis with policy limits, terms, and conditions to the current in-force program for the policy period November 20th, 2026 through November 20th, 2027 with a not-to-exceed premium of $741,500 ... It carries four to zero.
